title: scopeCacheKey returns 'unrestricted' for an admin caller with no project filter
description: scopeCacheKey (dashboard-metrics/index.js) is the Redis cache key discriminator for GET /api/dashboard/metrics. An admin caller who supplies no ?projectIds= resolves to projectScope={} (org-wide), which must map to the literal string 'unrestricted'.
steps: Call scopeCacheKey({}) directly with an empty projectScope object

title: scopeCacheKey produces the same key for the same project-ID set regardless of input order
description: For a non-admin, projectScope.projectId is {$in:[ObjectId,...]}. scopeCacheKey must sort+join the stringified IDs so ['B','A'] and ['A','B'] hash to the same cache entry, and two different ID sets must never collapse to the same key (guards the previously-fixed '[object Object]' collision across non-admins).
steps: Call scopeCacheKey({ projectId: { $in: [oidC] } }) with a disjoint project set
expectedResult: The first two calls return an identical string; the third call returns a different string from the first two.

title: fetchFrameworkReadiness buckets a framework by its own coveredThreshold/partialThreshold, defaulting to 70/30
description: Framework Board's readyCount/inProgressCount/earlyCount/notStartedCount come from comparing each framework's averaged coverage score against its own ClientFramework.coveredThreshold/partialThreshold, not a fixed >=90/>=50 split. A ClientFramework document with no threshold fields set must default to coveredThreshold=70, partialThreshold=30.
steps: Build a complianceList entry with averageScore=72 for a framework whose ClientFramework doc has no coveredThreshold/partialThreshold set
Run fetchFrameworkReadiness's bucketing logic against it
expectedResult: The framework is counted in readyCount (72 >= default coveredThreshold 70), not inProgressCount.

title: averageCompliance is weighted by each project's totalRequirements, not a plain per-project average
description: fetchComplianceMetrics sums overallScore*totalRequirements across all client_compliance_summary docs and divides by total totalRequirements, so a 5-requirement project can't swing the org-wide score as much as a 500-requirement project. Falls back to a plain average only when total totalRequirements across all summaries is 0.
steps: Supply two summaries: {overallScore:100, totalRequirements:5} and {overallScore:20, totalRequirements:500}
expectedResult: Result is close to 20 (weighted), not 60 (plain average of 100 and 20).

title: MiniSparkline renders a flat dashed placeholder instead of fabricating a trend from under 2 points
description: AuditOverviewContent.jsx's MiniSparkline treats data.length < 2 as 'not enough real history' and substitutes a flat 6-point placeholder array in grey (#A0AEC0) with a dashed stroke, rather than drawing a slope from a single real value. DEPRECATED: superseded by the Dashboard 2.0 rewrite (2026-08-13) — MiniSparkline no longer exists anywhere in the codebase. The replacement, miniCharts/Sparkline.jsx, has a different empty-state (a flat solid [{value:0},{value:0}] line, not a grey dashed placeholder), and in any case the board-level chartType/chartData/bottomData fields still computed in AuditOverviewContent.jsx are no longer read by OverviewModuleRail or ExecutiveSummaryBoardContent — that computation path is now dead code.
steps: Render MiniSparkline with data=[] and again with data=[42]
Inspect the rendered SVG path's stroke color and strokeDasharray
expectedResult: Both cases render the grey (#A0AEC0), dashed ('3,3'), flat placeholder line — never a colored, solid line implying a real trend.

title: AnimatedCounter preserves a non-numeric suffix while animating the numeric part from 0
description: AnimatedCounter (AuditOverviewContent.jsx) splits a rawValue like '72%' into numeric prefix 72 and suffix '%' via regex, animates 0->72, and re-appends the suffix on every frame so the displayed string never drops the '%'.
steps: Sample the displayed text mid-animation and after it settles
expectedResult: Every sampled frame ends in '%'; the final settled value reads exactly '72%'.

title: dateRangeFromPreset computes dateFrom/dateTo for 7d/30d/90d and returns {} for 'all' and 'custom'
description: DashboardFilterBar.jsx's dateRangeFromPreset maps a preset string to a concrete {dateFrom, dateTo} ISO-date pair by subtracting days from today; 'all' and 'custom' intentionally return an empty object so the caller keeps whatever explicit dates are already set.
expectedResult: '30d' returns {dateFrom: today-30d, dateTo: today} in YYYY-MM-DD; 'all' and 'custom' both return {}.

title: pctHealth buckets a percentage into critical/warning/good at the <40/<70 thresholds and returns 'unknown' for null/NaN
description: AuditOverviewContent.jsx's pctHealth(pct) — new in the Dashboard 2.0 rewrite — is the single shared health classifier for every board whose headline is itself a 0-100 score (Compliance Board, Risk Board, Framework Board's weakest-framework read). It drives each board's rail health dot color and the Summary board's composite-score ring via SummaryPostureHero's HEALTH_POINTS mapping, so an off-by-one at the threshold boundary would misclassify a board's status color across the whole module.
steps: Call pctHealth(39.9), pctHealth(40), pctHealth(69.9), pctHealth(70), pctHealth(100)

title: overviewHex falls back to the 'unknown' neutral hex for an unrecognized color family and selects light/dark by colorMode
description: overviewPalette.js's overviewHex(colorMode, family) looks up OVERVIEW_COLORS[family], falling back to OVERVIEW_COLORS.unknown when family isn't one of red/green/blue/amber/unknown. OverviewModuleRail's HEALTH_COLORS map and SummaryPostureHero's scoreColorHex both depend on this fallback never throwing or returning undefined for an unexpected input.
expectedResult: First two calls return OVERVIEW_COLORS.red.light ('#E53E3E') and .dark ('#C4787A') respectively; the third call returns OVERVIEW_COLORS.unknown.light ('#A0AEC0') rather than undefined or throwing.

title: SummaryPostureHero's composite score averages only boards with a known health state, excluding 'unknown' boards entirely rather than scoring them 0
description: SummaryPostureHero.jsx's compositeScore useMemo maps each board's health to HEALTH_POINTS (good=92, warning=55, critical=18) and averages only the boards where HEALTH_POINTS[health] is defined — a board with health='unknown' (e.g. Framework Board with zero active frameworks) is dropped from both the numerator and denominator, not counted as a 0-point board that would unfairly drag the composite down.
steps: Read the rendered composite score in the ring
expectedResult: Composite score is round((92+18)/2) = 55 — board C ('unknown') is excluded from the average, not averaged in as 0 (which would instead yield 37).
